grammar_details.focus: Passive Voice (Present & Past Simple), Tag Questions, and Compound Sentences

rules.formula: Present: am/is/are + past participle (V3)  |  Past: was/were + past participle (V3)
rules.usage: When the receiver of the action is more important than the doer, or when the agent is unknown or obvious.
examples: Elderly people are respected by all family members.
The nursing home was established thirty years ago.

rules.formula: Positive statement + negative tag?  |  Negative statement + positive tag?
examples: Grandparents tell wonderful stories, don't they?
The children weren't impolite yesterday, were they?

rules.formula: Independent clause + , (comma) + and / but / or / so + Independent clause
examples: Ali was very tired after practice, so he went to bed early.
Mina studied hard for the test, but she was a little nervous.

rules: A compound sentence connects two complete thoughts (independent clauses).
Always place a comma before the coordinating conjunction (and, but, or, so).
Do not use a comma when conjunctions merely join two words or phrases (e.g. 'He is kind and generous' - no comma).

vocab_development.rules: Words that frequently go together naturally in English: pay respect, show appreciation, take care of, burst into tears, make a mistake, do research, give advice, have regard for.
examples: pay + respect = pay respect
show + appreciation = show appreciation
burst + into tears = burst into tears

see_also.rules: Falling intonation on the tag when the speaker expects agreement (You know him, don't you? \). Rising intonation on the tag when the speaker is asking a genuine question (You didn't see him, did you? /).

lessons.title: Look it Up!
lessons.theme: Dictionaries, reference books, encyclopedia, vocabulary acquisition

grammar_details.focus: Passive with Modals, Defining Relative Clauses, and Conditional Type 2

rules.formula: Subject + modal (can, should, must, may) + be + past participle (V3)
examples: Unfamiliar words can be looked up in a bilingual dictionary.
English dictionaries must be arranged in alphabetical order.

rules.formula: who / that (for people)  |  which / that (for things)
rules.usage: Provides essential information to identify the preceding noun.
examples: A lexicographer is a person who writes dictionaries.
An encyclopedia is a book which gives information on many topics.

rules.formula: If + Simple Past, would / could + base verb
rules.usage: Hypothetical, unreal, or imaginary situations in the present or future.
examples: If I had more free time, I would read an English novel.
If she knew the phonetic symbols, she could pronounce words easily.

rules: Unity: All sentences in a paragraph must relate directly to the single controlling idea stated in the topic sentence.
Coherence: Sentences must follow a logical order with clear transitions and consistent pronouns.
Always eliminate irrelevant sentences that distract from the main idea.

vocab_development.topic: Prefixes inter- and multi- & Phrasal Verbs
vocab_development.rules: Prefix inter- means 'between' or 'among' (international, internet, interaction). Prefix multi- means 'many' (multilingual, multimedia, multicultural). Phrasal verbs combine verb + preposition/adverb (look up, figure out, give up, turn on, put off).
examples: international
multilingual
look up a word
figure out meaning

see_also.rules: Guide words printed at the top of a dictionary page indicate the first and last words on that page to assist quick alphabetical scanning.

lessons.title: Renewable Energy
lessons.theme: Clean energy, solar power, wind turbines, environmental protection

grammar_details.focus: Past Perfect Tense & Passive Voice Across All Tenses

rules.usage: An action completed before another past event or past point in time.
examples: Scientists had warned about air pollution before governments invested in solar energy.
By the time the sun set, the solar panels had generated enough electricity.

rules.formula: Present Perfect Passive: have/has been + V3  |  Past Perfect Passive: had been + V3
examples: Wind turbines have been installed in windy plains.
Fossil fuels had been consumed for decades before clean alternatives were developed.

rules: A concluding sentence signals the end of the paragraph.
Three effective concluding strategies: 1) Restate the topic sentence in different words; 2) Summarize main supporting points; 3) Provide a final thought or prediction.
Use transition signals: 'in conclusion', 'in short', 'overall', 'as a result'.

vocab_development.rules: Words derived from the same base root: pollute (verb) -> pollution (noun) -> pollutant (noun agent); consume (verb) -> consumption (noun) -> consumer (noun agent); generate (verb) -> generation (noun) -> generator (noun agent).
examples: pollute -> pollution
consume -> consumption
generate -> generator

see_also.topic: Pronunciation of Technical Terms & Stress Shift
see_also.rules: Notice stress shift across word families: 'energy (noun) vs ener'getic (adj); 'photograph vs pho'tography.

passages.title: Respecting Our Elders
passages.content: Elders play an essential and honored role in Iranian families and society. Grandparents are sources of wisdom, patience, and warmth. Many elderly people face health problems and need extra care as they age. In some countries, older people live alone or in nursing homes, but in our culture, families take care of their aging parents at home. Parents spend their entire lives working hard with endless love and devotion for their children. It is our moral duty to treat them with kindness, respect, and gratitude. Taking time to visit elderly relatives, listening to their memories, and valuing their advice brings blessing, unity, and happiness to the family.

passages.title: Volunteering at a Nursing Home
passages.content: Omid: 'Dr. Asadi, what were the young volunteers doing when I arrived at the nursing home?' Dr. Asadi: 'They were reading books to elderly residents and listening to their stories.' Omid: 'Do older people feel lonely in nursing centers?' Dr. Asadi: 'Yes, elderly people need affection and attention even more than medicine. Visiting them and showing appreciation brings great happiness to their hearts.'

passages.title: Dictionaries: Essential Tools for Language Learners
passages.content: A dictionary is an essential reference book that lists the words of a language in alphabetical order and gives their meanings, pronunciations, and grammatical functions. There are two main types of dictionaries: bilingual and monolingual. Bilingual dictionaries translate words from one language into another, which is helpful for beginners. Monolingual dictionaries explain words in the same language and are more suitable for intermediate and advanced learners. When you look up a word, you can find its definition, part of speech, phonetic transcription, syllables, and sample sentences. Dictionaries also list collocations, synonyms, antonyms, and idioms, which help you use words correctly and naturally.

passages.title: How to Choose a Good Dictionary
passages.content: Hamid: 'Mr. Ahmadi, should I buy a bilingual or a monolingual dictionary for Grade 12?' Mr. Ahmadi: 'A good learner's dictionary is ideal. It explains meanings in simple English and provides natural collocations.' Hamid: 'How can guide words help me?' Mr. Ahmadi: 'Guide words at the top of each page show the first and last entries, so you can locate words quickly without scanning every line.'

passages.title: Clean and Renewable Energy
passages.content: Energy is the driving force behind modern civilization, powering our homes, factories, and transportation. For over a century, the world has heavily relied on fossil fuels like coal, oil, and natural gas. However, fossil fuels are limited natural resources that will eventually run out, and burning them produces huge amounts of carbon dioxide and harmful air pollution that cause global warming. To protect our planet, scientists and governments are turning to renewable energy resources. Clean sources such as solar power, wind energy, hydroelectric power, and tidal energy generate electricity without polluting the environment. Solar panels absorb sunlight, and giant wind turbines turn wind currents into clean electrical power. Developing renewable energy is vital for a sustainable future.

passages.title: Visiting a Solar Power Plant
passages.content: Engineer: 'Welcome to Yazd Solar Power Station, students!' Student: 'How do these giant panels produce electricity?' Engineer: 'Photovoltaic cells absorb sunlight and convert it directly into clean electrical current.' Student: 'Can renewable energy completely replace fossil fuels in the future?' Engineer: 'Yes, by combining solar power, wind turbines, and hydroelectric dams, we can generate all our electricity without polluting the atmosphere.'
